chapter: Fellow musicians: Kirk, Bunk, Parker, McShann
title: Playing with Jay McShann at Wolf's Tavern
summary: Goodwin worked with McShann as guitarist and vocalist at Wolf's Tavern, and Smith calls McShann a true exponent of Kansas City jazz.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving

blocks.x: I was thinking about the next person Jay McShann, I want to talk about, W McSham for example.

Well Jis out of Muskogee, Oklahoma. He came here at a very young age. I was playing with Jay I guess back in the early '30s when Jay was playing -- we both were playing small nightclubs and we got together and we played at a place called Wolf's Tavern.
Who was the leader of the band?
Jay and you were his guitar player and vocalist. Wolf's Tavern, right downtown.
18th and Vine Streets and we played there for a while and I did quite a bit of work like that. I worked with Emil Williams like that, playing guitar and vocal.

Well, I never knew Emil but Jis a dear friend of mine and just a beautiful guy and it seems to me the numbers that he's written and the music he's played, that's Kansas City Jazz. Well, he got some experience from Jay McShann.
